question.problem: Given that $f(x)={5}^{x}+2{e}^{x}-\operatorname{ln}⁡2$,  find the slope of the tangent at $x=1.$
question.worked_solution:
Applying the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({5}^{x}+2{e}^{x}-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({5}^{x})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{e}^{x})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & ={5}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡5+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})+0 \\  & ={5}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡5+2{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & =({5}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡5+2{e}^{x}){|}_{x=1} \\  & ={5}^{1}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡5+2\cdot {e}^{1} \\  & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡5+2e.\end{aligned}
$$
